vpnServiceProvider.label: VPN provider
vpnServiceProvider.help: gluetun's identifier for your VPN service. Not listed? Type it anyway — gluetun recognizes more providers than this, and Extra environment variables (below) covers anything the form doesn't model yet.

wireguardAddresses.label: WireGuard interface address
wireguardAddresses.help: Required for Mullvad: the CIDR address from Mullvad's own config generator — the same for every Mullvad server and tied to your private key. Most other WireGuard providers derive this on their own and don't need it set.

serverCountries.label: Server countries
serverCountries.help: e.g. Netherlands. Leave blank to let the provider pick.

serverCategories.label: Server categories
serverCategories.help: e.g. P2P. Provider-specific — leave blank if yours doesn't use categories.

serverHostnames.label: Preferred server hostnames
serverHostnames.help: This is the list a VPN healer would cycle through in a later phase.

serverRegions.label: Server regions
serverRegions.help: Private Internet Access identifies servers by region rather than country, e.g. us_east. Leave blank to let PIA pick.

image.label: Image
image.help: Any tag on qmcgaw/gluetun. Use "Check for updates" on this card to pull it and recreate only if it actually changed.

containerName.label: Container name
containerName.help: Defaults to the Suite's container prefix followed by gluetun (streamshare-suite-gluetun unless overridden). Point it at a container you already run and the Suite will adopt that one instead of creating a second.
containerName.patternMessage: Use letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" only, starting with a letter or digit.

networks.label: Docker networks to join
networks.help: Names of existing Docker networks, e.g. vpnnet, ssbackend. The first one becomes the container's primary network. Defaults to the streamshare network the Suite's own compose file already declares — change this only to also join a stack of your own.

extraEnv.label: Extra environment variables
extraEnv.help: One KEY=VALUE per line, passed straight to the container. For a provider whose fields aren't modeled above yet — not validated, and a named field above always wins if it sets the same key.

mode.label: Where it runs
mode.help: Let the Suite run a PostgreSQL container, or point at a server you already have.

host.label: Host
host.help: Hostname or address the instances (and the Suite) reach the server at. Its port defaults to 5432 and is set in Advanced, below.

adminUser.label: Administrator username
adminUser.help: Must be able to CREATE DATABASE and CREATE ROLE. For a managed server this is the superuser it is created with.

adminPassword.label: Administrator password
adminPassword.help: Required for a server the Suite runs — the postgres image refuses to start without one. Optional for an external server using trust or peer authentication.

containerName.label: Container name
containerName.help: Defaults to the Suite's container prefix followed by postgres (streamshare-suite-postgres unless overridden). Point it at a container you already run and the Suite will adopt that one instead of creating a second.
containerName.patternMessage: Use letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" only, starting with a letter or digit.

image.label: Image
image.help: Any postgres tag. Changing this recreates the container; it does not migrate the data directory, so do not cross a major version this way.

networks.label: Docker networks to join
networks.help: Must include the network your instances reach the database over. Defaults to the streamshare network the Suite's own compose file already declares — change this only if your instances need to reach it over a stack of your own instead.

displayName.label: Name
displayName.help: How this provider appears in the dashboard, e.g. "Provider 1".

providerType.label: Playlist source
providerType.help: Xtream unlocks VOD, series, EPG and subscription status. Pick M3U only if your provider doesn't offer an Xtream API.

xtreamBaseUrl.label: Xtream base URL
xtreamBaseUrl.help: Your provider's portal address and port, e.g. http://provider.example:8080

ldapRequiredGroup.label: Required group
ldapRequiredGroup.help: Only members of this group may sign in.

publicBaseUrl.label: Public base URL
publicBaseUrl.help: The address your players reach this instance at, e.g. https://tv.example.com/provider-1. Leave blank if it is not published externally.

timezone.label: Timezone
timezone.help: Must match your players' timezone — catchup depends on it.

discordAdminRoleId.label: Admin role ID
discordAdminRoleId.help: Optional. A Discord role ID granted admin-level bot commands.

vodCacheEnabled.label: Cache VOD locally
vodCacheEnabled.help: Stores the VOD streams on the Docker host temporarily for faster and uninterrupted access.

catchupEnabled.label: Buffer live channels for catchup
catchupEnabled.help: Adds catchup (pause and rewind) functionality to any channel if not already offered by the provider. Starts buffering when a channel is first viewed, and keeps the last few hours of it.

catalogStorage.label: Keep provider catalogue on
catalogStorage.help: Memory is fastest, but RAM grows with the provider's catalogue (over 700 MB for a very large one). Disk uses far less RAM (around 90 MB) and needs about 2-3 times the catalogue size in the cache folder, with slightly slower searches.

cachePath.label: Cache location on the host
cachePath.help: Where this instance's VOD, catchup and disk catalogue cache lives on the Docker host. Leave blank to use a folder inside the Suite's data directory, which the Suite creates for you. A cache can grow to tens of gigabytes, so we recommend your own path on a disk meant for caching, with that much space free. If the folder does not exist yet, the Suite creates it owned by PUID/PGID from the Suite's compose file. An existing folder that has files in it, or is owned by anyone but root, keeps its owner, so it must be writable for that user.

healthCheckEnabled.label: Watch this instance's provider
healthCheckEnabled.help: Lets the VPN watchdog (see the VPN page) reconnect the tunnel when this instance's provider blocks the current exit IP.

healthCheckStreamId.label: Probe channel id
healthCheckStreamId.help: A live channel id from your provider (as it appears in a stream URL) that the instance requests periodically to tell whether the provider is blocking this exit IP. Type a channel name to search, or enter the id directly.

healthCheckBlockedCodes.label: Status codes indicating a block
healthCheckBlockedCodes.help: HTTP status codes your provider returns when it's blocking this exit IP. Defaults to 456 (the common Xtream convention) when left blank.

errorSlateEnabled.label: Show error slates
errorSlateEnabled.help: Streams a synthetic error slate to viewers instead of failing outright when the upstream provider errors.

errorSlateMessages.label: Custom messages
errorSlateMessages.help: Override the default message shown for a numeric HTTP status code, or for a connection-level failure with no status code of its own: UNREACHABLE, TIMEOUT, DNS, or TLS; or NO_RECORDING for catchup with no recording at the requested time, or IN_USE when every connection is taken by other viewers. Leave a code out to keep its default.

errorSlateRetryMaxMinutes.label: Retry for (minutes)
errorSlateRetryMaxMinutes.help: How long to keep retrying the upstream provider behind the slate before giving up on that request.

image.label: Image
image.help: Use "Check for updates" on this instance to pull this tag and recreate only if it actually changed.

containerName.label: Container name
containerName.help: Defaults to the Suite's container prefix followed by this instance's slug — see the preview above the Create button. Point it at a container you already run and the Suite will adopt that one instead of creating a second.
containerName.patternMessage: Use letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" only, starting with a letter or digit.

port.label: Port
port.help: Allocated automatically from the instance port range set under Stack. Change it only if something else on this host already uses the allocated one.

fallbacks.label: Fallback instances
fallbacks.help: When a live channel cannot start on this instance (its provider fails, or all its connections are in use by other viewers), try these instances in order. Each one serves the channel only while it has a free provider connection of its own.

extraEnv.label: Extra environment variables
extraEnv.help: One KEY=VALUE per line, passed straight to the container — for any stream-share setting not modelled above. Not validated, and a field above always wins if it sets the same key.

tlsMode.label: HTTPS
tlsMode.help: "Self-signed" issues a certificate from Caddy's own internal CA — browsers warn once, fine on a private network. "Automatic (ACME)" gets a real, trusted certificate per hostname, but needs ports 80 and 443 reachable from the internet and each hostname's DNS already pointed here. "Automatic (DNS challenge)" gets the same kind of certificate by proving domain ownership through your DNS provider's API instead, so no inbound ports are needed. Caddy adds your provider's plugin itself when it starts.

acmeEmail.label: ACME contact email
acmeEmail.help: Sent to your certificate authority for expiry notices only — never published anywhere.

dnsModule.label: Caddy module
dnsModule.help: The Go package of your provider's Caddy plugin, pinned to an exact version — e.g. github.com/caddy-dns/hetzner@v2.0.1 or github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare@v0.2.4. Without a pinned version, Caddy's add-package can build the module's unreleased branch instead of its latest release. See caddyserver.com/download for the full list of packages.

dnsDirective.label: Directive
dnsDirective.help: Everything after `dns` in the site's tls block, e.g. `hetzner {env.HETZNER_API_TOKEN}` or `cloudflare {env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}`. Reference credentials as {env.NAME} — a matching box appears below for each one, for you to fill in.

dnsEnv.label: Provider environment variables
dnsEnv.help: Filled in automatically from the {env.NAME} names in Directive, above. Stored write-only and passed to the Caddy container's environment; never written into the Caddyfile.

dnsPropagationDelay.label: Propagation delay
dnsPropagationDelay.help: Optional. How long to wait after creating the DNS record before asking the CA to check it, e.g. 30s. Slow DNS providers sometimes need this. Leave blank to use Caddy's default.

dashboardUrl.label: Dashboard public URL
dashboardUrl.help: Optional. The address this dashboard is reached at from outside, e.g. https://suite.example.com. Only the hostname (and port, if any) is used — give it a hostname of its own rather than a path. Leave blank to keep the dashboard unpublished. The Suite must be on a Docker network Caddy joins (the default streamshare network covers this). Publishing it puts the sign-in page on the internet: it has a real login, CSRF protection and a throttled sign-in, but that is now your exposure.

networks.label: Docker networks to join
networks.help: Must include whatever network gluetun and your instances are reachable on. Defaults to the streamshare network the Suite's own compose file already declares.

httpPort.label: HTTP port
httpPort.help: The host port Caddy answers plain HTTP on (and redirects to HTTPS from, in ACME mode).

image.label: Image
image.help: Any Caddy 2 tag. In DNS-challenge mode Caddy adds your provider's plugin itself on start (an image that already includes it skips the download); the image must not set its own ENTRYPOINT then.

containerName.label: Container name
containerName.help: Defaults to the Suite's container prefix followed by caddy (streamshare-suite-caddy unless overridden). Point it at a container you already run and the Suite will adopt that one instead of creating a second.
containerName.patternMessage: Use letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" only, starting with a letter or digit.

extraCaddyfile.label: Extra Caddyfile
extraCaddyfile.help: Raw Caddyfile text appended after every generated site block — for anything the Suite doesn't render for you, such as a route to something it doesn't manage. In JSON format.

gluetun.label: Gluetun (VPN)
gluetun.description: The VPN tunnel. When enabled, every StreamShare instance shares its network namespace and is published through it, so replacing it briefly takes them with it. When disabled, every container gets its own network and publishes its own port.

postgres.label: PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Where every instance keeps its history, VOD index and aliases. Each instance gets a database of its own rather than sharing one.

instance.label: StreamShare instance
instance.description: One IPTV provider, shared with your users.

caddy.label: Caddy (reverse proxy)
caddy.description: Publishes any instance with a public base URL under a real hostname, with HTTPS handled for you.

nav.signOutBody: You'll need to sign in again to get back in.

signIn.createIntro: This is the only account. Nothing else works until it exists.
signIn.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. There is no recovery — store it somewhere safe.
signIn.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.rejectedNote: The provider is rejecting this instance's credentials
subscription.lastGoodError: Showing the last successful read — refresh failed: {{error}}

directiveEnv.hint: Reference a credential in Directive above as {{ref}} to get a box for it here.

errorSlates.empty: No overrides — every code shows its default message.

providerCredentials.needXtream: Enter the Xtream username and password first
providerCredentials.confirmBody: Sets this instance's sign-in to the same username and password as its Xtream provider account immediately, no need to hit Save afterwards. Any custom username/password stops working right away.

highlights.instances: Add your IPTV provider(s) as instances — each gets its own container, database and API key, set up for you.
highlights.caching: Turn on VOD caching and catchup buffering, per instance.
highlights.external: Make an instance reachable from outside your network, with HTTPS handled automatically if you want it.
highlights.vpn: Route everything through a VPN, shared across every instance.
highlights.health: Watch instance health and have the VPN reconnect itself when a provider blocks it.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.intro: A few short steps get StreamShare Suite fully configured. Answer what you know; anything you leave blank keeps a sensible default, and everything here can be changed again later from Settings or the Stack page. Don't worry, nothing will be changed or created until you hit "Apply" on the Stack page at the end of the setup.

done.title: You're set up!
done.body: Don't worry, nothing will actually be applied yet. In the stack plan, review the setup and hit apply if you're satisfied. You can always change anything from the Stack page or just re-run the wizard.

database.intro: Where every instance keeps stuff like its history, VOD index and aliases. Each instance gets its own database, created automatically.

portRange.title: Instance port range
portRange.intro: Let's start with a port range. Each instance gets its own port, allocated from a band of 20 starting here. Only worth changing if that range is already taken by something else on the host.

vpn.title: Route traffic through a VPN?
vpn.intro: Recommended if your provider restricts access by location or IP. StreamShare Suite sets up a Gluetun instance for you. Every instance shares this tunnel. You will probably need an account with a supported VPN provider. Read all about it <wiki>over here</wiki>.
vpn.gluetunHelp: The tunnel every instance's traffic will route through.

features.intro: Special features offered by StreamShare. Here you can set up stuff like caching and buffering. The folder below is where an instance keeps its temporary files: VOD cache and catchup buffers.
features.helper: Helper: you may enter a parent folder on the Docker host here which will then be used as the parent folder for instances below. Only instances that don't already have a files path set are affected. Subfolders will be appended automatically.
features.pathNote: Leave the paths below blank to keep each cache in the Suite's own data folder. Caches can grow to tens of gigabytes, so we recommend an absolute path on a disk meant for caching with that much room free. If the folder does not exist yet, the Suite creates it for the PUID/PGID the Suite runs as. An existing folder keeps its owner, so it must be writable for that user.
features.cachePath: Temporary files location on this host

health.intro: Optional. Lets the VPN watchdog reconnect the tunnel when a provider blocks the current exit IP — pick which instances to take into account.
health.probeHelp: In order for the health check to work, you need to specify a channel to probe for each instance. This channel will be synthetically 'viewed' to see if it's accessible. Type a channel name to search and pick a result, or enter a stream ID directly if you already know it.
health.checkTimes: Check times (local) — usually twice a day should be enough. Pick times that are usually outside of your own viewing hours, so the health check doesn't interfere with you watching.

access.intro: Completely optional. Allows you to reach the instances from outside your local network. You're responsible for the DNS/routing part — this just tells each instance what its own externally-reachable address is.
access.tokenSet: A token is set. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
access.caddyTitle: Reach these URLs from your local network?
access.caddyHelp: This is what Caddy is for. It redirects the URL you enter above to the right instance and port. Beware: you're still responsible for pointing that URL's DNS at this host; you will most likely need your own DNS server for this (like AdGuard Home or Pi-hole).

provider.label: Use my provider credentials
provider.help: Simplest option — everyone signs in with the same Xtream username and password typed in above.

custom.label: Set custom credentials
custom.help: A separate username and password from your provider's, for connecting without handing out the real ones.

ldap.label: Use LDAP
ldap.help: Sign in against an existing directory server instead — for handing out per-user access.

xtream.help: Unlocks VOD, series, EPG and subscription status. Use this if your provider offers an Xtream API — most do.

m3u.help: Just a playlist link, no Xtream API. Live channels work; no VOD/series/EPG or subscription status.

instances.title: Your instances
instances.intro: Now let's set up a StreamShare instance, one per IPTV provider. At least one is required. To remove an instance, use the Stack page instead — it's not available here because reasons.
instances.addOne: Add at least one instance to continue

stack.dockerUnreachable: Can't reach the Docker socket proxy. Set DOCKER_PROXY_URL, or check that the docker-socket-proxy service is running and reachable.

card.checkUpdatesTitle: Check and pull the latest version of {{name}}'s configured image tag and recreate if it actually changed
card.takeoverNote: A container by this name is already running without the Suite's labels. It stays untouched unless you replace it with a managed one.

caddy.suiteContainerHint: Detected automatically. Caddy reaches the dashboard at this name.

history.confirmBody: This replaces the currently saved configuration with this earlier one. Nothing is applied to Docker until you Apply.

import.title: Import from running containers
import.intro: Finds gluetun, PostgreSQL and StreamShare containers already running outside the Suite and reads their real configuration in, instead of retyping it by hand. The containers themselves are never touched.
import.none: Nothing found that isn't already part of the stack.

connect.title: Point your IPTV client at these
connect.body: The internal URL only works from this host or if you have access to your local network. The public URL is the one you use to set up on your mobile devices to be able to connect elsewhere. If you have Caddy set up, then you can use the public URL within your local network as well.
connect.internalAddress: <Your Docker host's IP address or hostname>:{{port}}

instances.title: Instances
instances.subtitle: Create one per IPTV provider. Ports are allocated from {{first}}–{{last}}.
instances.empty: No instances yet. Adding one creates its container and its database automagically.
instances.checkUpdatesTitle: Check and pull the latest version of this instance's configured image tag and recreate if it actually changed

portRange.title: Instance port range
portRange.description: Instances are allocated {{size}} ports starting here (currently {{start}}–{{end}}). Instances already inside the range keep their port; any that fall outside the new range move to a free port in it.

removeDialog.title: Remove {{name}}?
removeDialog.body: This takes it out of the stack. Its container keeps running until you apply the plan, which will then offer to remove it.
removeDialog.dropDatabase: Also drop {{database}} and its role. This deletes its watch history permanently. Leave it unticked to keep the data.

plan.title: Stack plan
plan.emptySwitchedOff_one: Nothing in the stack right now — {{list}} is switched off. Turn the VPN back on under the Components tab to manage it again.
plan.emptySwitchedOff_other: Nothing in the stack right now — {{list}} are switched off. Turn the VPN back on under the Components tab to manage it again.
plan.emptyFresh: Nothing in the stack yet. Configure a component under the Components tab to get started, or run the <setup>setup wizard</setup> for a guided walkthrough.
plan.removeBody: {{name}} was created by the Suite but is no longer part of your stack. Removing it stops and deletes the container.

overview.nothingPlayingHint: Active streams across every instance will show up here.

instances.none: No instances configured. Set INSTANCE_1_NAME / INSTANCE_1_URL / INSTANCE_1_API_KEY (and _2_, _3_, …) in the dashboard's environment.

aliases.intro: Give a friendly name to viewers that show up by IP address (e.g. when an instance has LDAP disabled). An alias means the same thing everywhere, but each instance stores its own copy — this saves it to every instance at once by default, and the underlying IP is still what's actually used to identify the viewer.
aliases.prefill: Adding an alias for {{ip}} — pick a name below.
aliases.emptyHint: Add one above to give a friendly name to a viewer that currently shows up by IP address.

history.emptyHint: Try a wider time range, or check back once someone starts watching.

users.emptyHint: Users show up here once they connect to a stream-share instance.

vod.shareLinksHint: Need a live channel link for a time window? Use <link>Share links</link>.
vod.searchPlaceholder: Search movies and series across all instances…
vod.initialTitle: Search for a movie or series
vod.initialHint: Results are pulled live from every instance that has an Xtream provider configured — nothing is indexed or stored here.
vod.noResultsHint: Try a different title or spelling.

general.title: General
general.siteTitleHint: Shown in the sidebar and the browser tab.
general.pollHint: How often the browser re-polls. Minimum 5000.
general.timeoutHint: How long to wait for one instance before giving up on it.
general.autoCheckHint: Once a day the Suite asks GitHub for the latest release of itself, StreamShare, gluetun and Caddy. Nothing is downloaded or changed.
general.checksFailed: Some checks failed. The Suite retries within the hour.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.description: Every credential, instance definition and component setting lives in one file. Download it before a risky change.
backup.restoreHint: Replaces everything currently stored — every credential and setting — with what's in the file. Signs everyone out.
backup.restored: Restored. Reload the page — you'll need to sign in again if this backup predates your session.
backup.confirmBody: This replaces every credential, instance definition and component setting currently stored with what's in the file, and will sign everyone out. This cannot be undone from here — make sure you have a current backup first if you want to keep what's there now.

password.title: Change password
password.description: Changing it signs out every other session and revokes the API token.

api.title: API access
api.description: Lets scripts and other tools interact with StreamShare Suite. Send the token as an Authorization: Bearer header.
api.newTokenHint: Copy it now. It will not be shown again.
api.confirmBody: Anything still using the current token will stop working immediately.

vpn.notConfiguredHint: Set GLUETUN_URL (e.g. http://gluetun:8000) — and GLUETUN_API_KEY if your control server requires one — in the dashboard's environment to enable this page.
vpn.reconnectNote: Reconnect stops the tunnel, waits for it to confirm, starts it again, and waits for a fresh exit IP — the dashboard refreshes every second while it works, and keeps doing so afterward until the exit IP card actually has a value.
vpn.stopBody: This disconnects gluetun. Any traffic routed through it (e.g. your stream-share instance's outbound connection) will be interrupted or exposed until it's started again.
vpn.reconnectBody: This stops and restarts the tunnel, the same as Stop followed by Start. Any traffic routed through it will be interrupted until it comes back up, which can take a while depending on your provider.

watchdog.title: VPN watchdog
watchdog.description: Probes every instance with health checking enabled, on a schedule, and reconnects the tunnel when one reports its provider is blocking the current exit IP.
watchdog.noTimes: At least one time is required.

shareLinks.vodHint: Need a movie or episode link? Use <link>VOD search</link>.
shareLinks.noPublicUrl: The Suite does not know this instance's public address, so it cannot build copyable links. Set the public base URL on the instance (Stack page) to enable Copy.
shareLinks.unsupported: This instance does not support share links
shareLinks.unsupportedHint: Update it to a newer image and reload.
shareLinks.emptyHint: Create one for a guest to watch a channel for a while.

windowProblem.pick: Pick a start and an end time.
windowProblem.order: The end must be after the start.
windowProblem.tooLong: A share link may last at most 24 hours.

dialog.pathsOnly: The Suite does not know this instance's public address, so these are paths only. Add your public address in front of them.
